cases.title: A terrain match becomes a field question
cases.supported: Generalized maps at this anchor describe Neoproterozoic sedimentary and volcaniclastic material. This supports a preliminary sedimentary fieldwork question.
cases.scope: Macrostrat unit 3306996/source 190 (BRGM–CGMW Africa 1:10,000,000) and unit 3193272/source 154 (generalized GSC world geology). Regional polygon intersections, not confirmed exposed outcrops or coverage across 24 km.
cases.contradiction: Mixed volcaniclastic material and regional map scale limit the interpretation. No cited evidence establishes a local lake, delta, carbonate-bearing outcrop or biosignature-preservation setting.
cases.independence: The two generalized maps may share source inputs. They are not two independent local observations.
cases.next_measurement: If access is permitted: local unit mapping and a GNSS-controlled transect; document bedding, grain size and sedimentary structures, then test mineral identity with petrography and Raman/XRD. XRF chemistry alone does not establish carbonate mineralogy.
cases.hypothesis: If permitted exposures confirm sedimentary material, a standardized transect may rehearse stratigraphic logging and evidence-preserving sample documentation.

cases.title: A high terrain score cannot establish geology
cases.supported: Real terrain and climate inputs support broad morphology and dry operating context. Regional maps identify Jurassic granitic and intrusive igneous material at the anchor.
cases.scope: Macrostrat unit 4973267/source 1087 (South America 1:5,000,000) and unit 3186158/source 154 (generalized world geology). These are mapped regional interpretations.
cases.contradiction: Mapped granitic/intrusive material does not establish the sedimentary, lacustrine or carbonate process required by this mission. Geology is not wholly unmapped; mission-specific relevance remains unassessed. High partial U does not resolve that gap.
cases.independence: Generalized geological maps and coarse climatology do not replace independent local sampling.
cases.next_measurement: Inspect detailed maps and permitted exposures for sedimentary cover. If only granitic material is confirmed, reject the sedimentary hypothesis or choose an appropriately limited navigation-workflow experiment.
cases.hypothesis: Field reconnaissance can test whether an accessible sedimentary exposure exists within the proposed research area; no positive geological result is predicted.

cases.role: Documented benchmark · excluded from discovery counts
cases.title: What direct process evidence adds
cases.supported: Published shoreline hydromagnesite and microbialite evidence supports a carbonate/lacustrine process analogy. The anchor matches the published sample-station location.
cases.scope: The source paper's station 2/type locality is 37°31′13.47″N,29°40′24.44″E. NASA's lake-level comparison does not characterize every rock across the 24 km terrain window.
cases.contradiction: Living biology and modern liquid water differ from present Mars. The terrain footprint includes surrounding rocks and water; lake-surface elevation is not bathymetry. Regional ophiolite polygons do not override direct shoreline literature or establish lunar basalt relevance.
cases.independence: A known benchmark illustrates direct process evidence. It is never an automatic discovery. C 100% means all declared model criteria are assessed, not complete scientific knowledge.
cases.next_measurement: Confirm access and sampling permissions; document the exact study boundary and compare sediment/mineral observations with published shoreline measurements.
cases.hypothesis: A permitted shoreline documentation exercise may test whether a sampling protocol preserves mineral, textural and contextual observations from carbonate deposits.
